citation.title: On the Foundations of the Design-Based Approach

standing_assumptions:
The work is a main article of 16 pages (Political Analysis (2026), 0, 1–16, doi:10.1017/pan.2026.10045; printed page = PDF page) and a publisher's Supplementary Appendix of 10 pages (publisher-supplement.pdf; printed page = PDF page, the first page unnumbered). The main text states no numbered theorem: its formal content is the setup of Section 3, Equations (1)–(8), Conditions 4.1, 5.1 and 5.2 and the worked Tables 1–5. The supplement carries its own Equations (1)–(11), Conditions 1.1–1.3 and Proposition 1; they are cited below as ‘supplement Equation (k)’ and so on. Everything quoted was read from the page images.
(S1) Probability space. p. 3, Section 3: “we formalize the design in terms of a probability triple $(\Omega,S,P)$, where the sample space, $\Omega$, consists of all conceivable experimental (or sampling) interventions and each realized intervention, $\omega$, refers to the vector of treatment (or sampling) assignments to all $N$ observations. The event space is the power set of the sample space, $S=\mathcal P(\Omega)$ and we assume that our probability measure satisfies $\Pr[A]=\sum_{\omega\in A}p(\omega),\ \forall A\in S$, where $p:\Omega\to[0,1]$, with $p(\omega)$ characterizing the probability of the assignment of an intervention.”
(S2) Design and design space. p. 3, Section 3.1: “We define the design space $\mathcal Z=\mathbf Z(\Omega)$, where $\mathbf Z$ is a bijective random vector $\mathbf Z:\Omega\to\mathbb R^N$. The design is defined as the joint p.m.f. of $\mathbf Z$, $f:\mathbb R^N\to[0,1]$. We may define all objects with respect to the design vector $\mathbf Z$, removing all notational dependence on $\omega$. We assume that the design is determined by the researcher”. ‘Bijective’ is read as injective, that is, a bijection of $\Omega$ onto $\mathcal Z$ (finding P061-N003, a clarity note); the inverse in Equation (1) is applied only on $\mathcal Z$. $\mathcal Z$ is the set of feasible interventions and may be strictly larger than the support of the design (p. 8: “$\mathcal Z$ may include assignments outside the design”).
(S3) Population and raw potential outcomes. p. 4, Section 3.2: “This finite population is indexed by $i=1,\ldots,N$, where indexing is fixed.” “We represent the outcomes of interest associated with these units with a real-valued random vector, $\mathbf Y$. The random vector $\mathbf Y$ characterizes the raw potential outcomes, which can be represented for each individual $i$ as $$y_i(\mathbf z)=Y_i(\mathbf Z^{-1}(\mathbf z)),\ \forall i\in 1,\ldots,N,\ \mathbf z\in\mathcal Z.\qquad(1)$$ The raw potential outcome $y_i(\mathbf z)$ for individual $i$ is what we observe if we perform intervention $\mathbf z$ and measure unit $i$’s outcome. There are a total of $N\times|\mathcal Z|$ raw potential outcomes in the causal setting.” The observed outcome is $Y_i=y_i(\mathbf Z)$ (supplement p. 2: “we use the fact that $Y_i=y_i(\mathbf Z)$, from the definition of raw potential outcomes given in Section 3”).
(S4) Exposure mapping. p. 4, Section 3.3: “Formally, our exposure mapping for individual $i$ is a function $g_i:\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R$.” “Given that we have knowledge of the support of the design vector, $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)$, we can define a function $g_i|_{\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)}:\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)\to\mathbb R$. We denote the $N$-length random exposure vector $$\mathbf D=(g_1(\mathbf Z),g_2(\mathbf Z),\ldots,g_N(\mathbf Z)).\qquad(2)$$” The mappings used in the paper's examples: the ‘individualistic’ mapping (p. 5) $g_i(\mathbf z)=\begin{cases}1&:z_i=1\\0&:\text{otherwise}\end{cases},\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,N\},\mathbf z\in\{0,1\}^N$ (written $g_i(\mathbf z)=z_i$ on p. 8); the network mapping (p. 5) $$g_i(\mathbf z)=\begin{cases}0\ (\text{Control})&:\text{ if }z_i=0\text{ and }\theta_i\mathbf z=0,\\1\ (\text{Isolated Direct})&:\text{ if }z_i=1\text{ and }\theta_i\mathbf z=0,\\2\ (\text{Indirect})&:\text{ if }z_i=0\text{ and }\theta_i\mathbf z>0,\\3\ (\text{Direct \& Indirect})&:\text{ if }z_i=1\text{ and }\theta_i\mathbf z>0,\end{cases}\quad\forall i\in\{1,\ldots,N\},\ \mathbf z\in\{0,1\}^N,\qquad(3)$$ “where $\theta_i$ is the $i$th row of the network adjacency matrix”; and the coarsened mapping of Section 6.2 (p. 11) $g_i(\mathbf z)=\begin{cases}1&:z_i>0\\0&:\text{otherwise}\end{cases},\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,N\},\mathbf z\in\{0,1,2\}^N$.
(S5) Exposure probability, positivity, EPO. p. 6, Section 4.1: “we denote the marginal probability that unit $i$ enters exposure $d$ under the design distribution of $\mathbf Z$ as $$\pi_i(d)=\Big(\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z):g_i(\mathbf z)=d}\Pr[\mathbf Z=\mathbf z]\Big)=\Pr[D_i=d].\qquad(4)$$” “Condition 4.1 (Individual positivity). An exposure $d$ satisfies individual positivity if there exists a $c$ such that $0<c\le\pi_i(d)\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$.” “Given that relevant individual positivity assumptions hold, the EPO for unit $i$ under exposure $d$ is defined as $$\overline y_i(d)=\frac{\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z):g_i(\mathbf z)=d}y_i(\mathbf z)\Pr[\mathbf Z=\mathbf z]}{\sum_{\mathbf z\in\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z):g_i(\mathbf z)=d}\Pr[\mathbf Z=\mathbf z]}=\mathrm E[y_i(\mathbf Z)|g_i(\mathbf Z)=d]=\mathrm E[y_i(\mathbf Z)|D_i=d].\qquad(5)$$” “To avoid notational overload, these definitions implicitly hold fixed the exposure mapping $g$ and design $\mathbf Z$.” Where two designs are compared the paper writes $\tau_{\mathbf Z}$, $\tau_{\mathbf Z'}$ (Tables 4 and 5, Section 6.3).
(S6) AEPO, EED, AEED. p. 7: “Under individual positivity (Condition 4.1) for exposure $d$ and all individuals $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, we average the EPOs over the units in the population to define the AEPO as $$\overline y(d)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\overline y_i(d)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\mathrm E[y_i(\mathbf Z)|D_i=d].\qquad(6)$$” “For an individual observation $i$, assuming that Condition 4.1 holds for exposures $d$ and $d'$ for all individuals $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$, we can define the EED between $d$ and $d'$ as $$\tau_i(d,d')=\overline y_i(d)-\overline y_i(d').\qquad(7)$$” “The AEED between $d$ and $d'$ is $$\tau(d,d')=\overline y(d)-\overline y(d')=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\tau_i(d,d').\qquad(8)$$” Footnote 8 (p. 7): “We compare this to the assignment-conditional unit-level treatment effect defined in Sävje, Aronow, and Hudgens (2021): $\tau_i^{AC}(d,d',\mathbf z_{-i})=y_i(d;\mathbf z_{-i})-y_i(d';\mathbf z_{-i})$. In the assignment-conditional unit-level treatment effect, we hold constant treatments assigned to all other individuals at $\mathbf z_{-i}$.”
(S7) Stability conditions. p. 8, Section 5.1: “Condition 5.1 (NURVA). $$g_i(\mathbf z)=g_i(\mathbf z')\implies y_i(\mathbf z)=y_i(\mathbf z')=\overline y_i(g_i(\mathbf z)),\ \forall\mathbf z,\mathbf z'\in\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z).$$” “Condition 5.2 (SUTVA). $$g_i(\mathbf z)=g_i(\mathbf z')\implies y_i(\mathbf z)=y_i(\mathbf z')=\overline y_i(g_i(\mathbf z)),\ \forall\mathbf z,\mathbf z'\in\mathcal Z.$$”
(S8) Estimator. Supplement p. 1: “Throughout, we will require the individual positivity, Condition 4.1, referenced in Section 4.” “We use the Horvitz-Thompson inverse probability weighted estimator (Horvitz and Thompson 1952), as defined in Equation 1, $$\hat{\overline y}(d)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{Y_i\mathbb 1\{D_i=d\}}{\pi_i(d)}.\qquad(1)$$” Supplement p. 4: “For the AEED, define $\hat\tau(d,d')=\hat{\overline y}(d)-\hat{\overline y}(d')$ and $\pi_{ij}(d,d')=\Pr[D_i=d,D_j=d']$.” Supplement p. 3: “Let the joint exposure probability, $\pi_{ij}(d)=\Pr[D_i=D_j=d]$.”
(S9) Asymptotic regime. Supplement p. 5: “We define a sequence of finite populations $U_{(N)}$ indexed by population size $N$. Associated with each finite population $U_{(N)}$ is a known random design vector $\mathbf Z_{(N)}$, a feasible intervention set $\mathcal Z_{(N)}$, $N$ exposure mappings $g_{i,(N)}:\mathcal Z_{(N)}\to\mathbb R$, and $N\times|\mathcal Z_{(N)}|$ raw potential outcomes. Assume that the range of $g_{i,(N)}|\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z_{(N)})$ contains $d$, for all $i,N$. The observed data is $(\mathbf Z_{(N)},\mathbf Y_{(N)})$. We let $N$ tend to infinity.” Note 2 (supplement p. 10): “In the asymptotic regime we could also index observations of, e.g., $y_i$ and $\pi_i(d)$ by $(N)$ but we leave this indexing implicit below.”
(S10) What the paper does not state, and how it is read here. (a) $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)$ is not defined; it is read as $\{\mathbf z\in\mathcal Z:\Pr[\mathbf Z=\mathbf z]>0\}$. (b) ‘Finite population’ restricts $N$, not the number of assignments: by (S1) the support is countable, and nothing makes it finite. Every design in the paper's examples and tables has finite support; the general setup admits a countably infinite support with unbounded outcomes (finding P061-CAND-001). (c) No integrability condition is stated anywhere. (d) Conditions 5.1 and 5.2 print no quantifier over $i$; they are read as holding for every $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Their last equality, $=\overline y_i(g_i(\mathbf z))$, involves an EPO that Equation (5) defines only when $\pi_i(g_i(\mathbf z))>0$: under Condition 5.1 this is automatic and the equality follows from the first one; under Condition 5.2 it is read as holding wherever the EPO is defined (finding P061-CAND-003, a clarity note, whose repair deletes that equality from Condition 5.2). (e) The notation $y_i(d;\mathbf z_{-i})$ of footnote 8 is not defined further; it is read as the raw potential outcome at the assignment vector whose $i$th coordinate is $d$ and whose other coordinates are $\mathbf z_{-i}$, which presupposes that the labels $d,d'$ are assignment coordinates and that the hybrid vector lies in $\mathcal Z$. (f) All probabilities, expectations, variances and covariances are over the design distribution of $\mathbf Z$, with the raw potential outcomes fixed.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Sections 1, 3.1 and 4, the description of the targets as ‘new’ or ‘novel’: the identities behind the corrected attribution (EPO and AEED as the expected exposure outcome and effect; individualistic binary AEED as the average distributional shift effect)
canonical_claim.location: p. 2 (PDF p. 2), p. 3 (PDF p. 3) and p. 5 (PDF p. 5) for the three sentences; Equations (5)–(8), pp. 6–7 (PDF pp. 6–7)
canonical_claim.statement:
Formal content of the corrected attribution. Sol's replacement text: ‘We formulate design-conditional inferential targets, building on the expected exposure outcomes and effects of Sävje (2024). Under individualistic binary exposure, the AEED is the average distributional shift effect of Sävje, Aronow, and Hudgens (2021).’ On a common domain, namely a population of $N>0$ units, a finite assignment set $S$ with probabilities $p_{\mathbf z}\ge0$, $\sum_{\mathbf z\in S}p_{\mathbf z}=1$, raw outcomes $y_i:S\to\mathbb R$, exposure mappings $g_i$ on $S$, $Y_i=y_i(\mathbf Z)$, $D_i=g_i(\mathbf Z)$, and exposures $a,b$ with $\pi_i(a)>0$ and $\pi_i(b)>0$ for all $i$:
(i) the EPO of Equation (5) is the conditional mean $$\overline y_i(d)=\sum_{\mathbf z\in S:g_i(\mathbf z)=d}y_i(\mathbf z)\,\frac{p_{\mathbf z}}{\pi_i(d)}=\mathrm E[y_i(\mathbf Z)\mid D_i=d],\qquad d\in\{a,b\},$$ which is the earlier expected exposure outcome;
(ii) the AEED of Equation (8) equals the earlier expected exposure effect: $$\tau(a,b)=\overline y(a)-\overline y(b)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\big[\overline y_i(a)-\overline y_i(b)\big];$$
(iii) for binary assignments $\mathbf z\in\{0,1\}^N$ and the individualistic mapping $g_i(\mathbf z)=z_i$, $$\tau(1,0)=\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N\big[\mathrm E(Y_i\mid Z_i=1)-\mathrm E(Y_i\mid Z_i=0)\big]=\tau_{\mathrm{ADSE}},$$ the average distributional shift effect.
These identities hold for every raw outcome schedule and every design on the common domain, with no SUTVA or NURVA assumption.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The paper's objects: $\pi_i(d)$ and the EPO, Equations (4)–(5), p. 6 (S5); AEPO, EED and AEED, Equations (6)–(8), p. 7 (S6); the individualistic mapping, p. 5 (S4). The three sentences corrected: p. 2 “In Section 4, we define a set of new inferential targets for the design-based setting.”; p. 3 “However, we will use this setup to define novel estimands in Section 4.”; p. 5 “We define new inferential targets for the design-based framework.” The earlier definitions are not in the staged sources; they are as recorded in the validator's source_notes.md from the public manuscripts it read: Sävje, arXiv 2103.06471v2 (the manuscript of the work published as Sävje 2024), Section 4.3, $\bar y_i(d)=\mathbb E\{y_i(\mathbf Z)\mid D_i=d\}$, and Definition 1, $\tau(a,b)=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n[\bar y_i(a)-\bar y_i(b)]$, for binary nominal treatments and arbitrary exposure mappings; Sävje, Aronow and Hudgens (2021), Definition 4, $\tau_{\mathrm{ADSE}}=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n[\mathbb E(Y_i\mid Z_i=1)-\mathbb E(Y_i\mid Z_i=0)]$.
canonical_claim.note: P061-N006 is rated an error, Moderate (ratings.json); Sol's verdict is confirmed in part, upheld on re-run. The finding is about attribution, not about a wrong formula: no equation of the paper changes, and the correction replaces ‘new’/‘novel’ by an explicit relation to the earlier constructions. It is on this list because the finding rests on exact identities between the paper's targets and the earlier ones, and the corrected sentence asserts one of them ((iii)); the brief makes the formal content of such a corrected claim a target. The identities are close to definitional: (i) is the definition of a conditional mean on a finite space, (ii) is Equation (8) itself, (iii) is (ii) with $D_i=Z_i$. A Lean statement certifies equality of the mathematical objects on the common domain and nothing about historical priority; the forms of the earlier definitions are hypotheses taken from the validator's source notes. The validator already proved these three identities in Lean for arbitrary finite assignment types (P061-N006/v1/artifact/check.lean, with lean-output.txt), noting that they hold there even without positivity because division is total in Lean; the statement above keeps the positivity under which the paper defines the objects. The validator's worked instance (check_exact.py) has the design and outcome rule of the paper's Table 1(a), one of two units treated with each outcome equal to the other unit's treatment: AEED and ADSE both equal $-1$, while every assignment-conditional own-treatment effect is zero, so footnote 8's distinction from the assignment-conditional effect stands. The finding does not establish that the wider framework, NURVA or the survey interpretation lack novelty.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Condition 4.1 and Equation (5), with Equations (6)–(8) and supplement Equation (3): positivity alone does not make the targets well-defined
canonical_claim.location: p. 6 (PDF p. 6) for Condition 4.1 and Equation (5); p. 7 (PDF p. 7) for Equations (6)–(8); Supplementary Appendix p. 2 (publisher-supplement.pdf p. 2) for supplement Equation (3)
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The probability triple and $p$: Section 3, p. 3 (S1). $\mathbf Z$, $\mathcal Z$: Section 3.1, p. 3 (S2); here $\mathbf Z$ is a bijection onto $\mathbb R^N$ with $N=1$, so the example does not depend on reading ‘bijective’ as injective. Raw potential outcomes: Equation (1), p. 4 (S3). Exposure mapping $g_i:\mathcal Z\to\mathbb R$: p. 4 (S4). $\pi_i(d)$, Condition 4.1 and Equation (5): p. 6 (S5). Equations (6)–(8): p. 7 (S6). Supplement Equations (1) and (3): pp. 1–2 (S8 and P061-T16). $x^+=\max(x,0)$, $x^-=\max(-x,0)$. ‘Does not exist’ means: the sum over the countable support is not absolutely convergent, equivalently the expectation is not defined as a Lebesgue integral (both the positive and the negative part are infinite). $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)$ as in (S10)(a).
canonical_claim.note: P061-CAND-001 is rated an error, Minor (ratings.json); Sol's verdict is confirmed, upheld on re-run. Steps 1–10 of the validator's derivation (check.py verifies the probabilities, the moment sums and the divergence symbolically). The example lies inside the stated general model and outside all of the paper's illustrated designs, which have finite support; it is an existence failure, not evidence of bias where the means exist, and it does not touch the finite examples, Tables 1–5, the NURVA results or supplement Proposition 1 (Condition 1.1 bounds the reweighted outcomes). In Lean the natural statements are: the family $k\mapsto y_1(k)p(k)$ is not summable over the positive integers (and its positive and negative parts each have unbounded partial sums), with (a)–(c) as exact identities; ‘the conditional expectation does not exist’ should be stated as non-summability, since Mathlib's integral and tsum return 0 for non-integrable or non-summable input and an equation written with them would be misleading. The first eight terms $k,\ p(k),\ y_1(k),\ p(k)y_1(k)$ in the validator's output are $1,\tfrac14,4,1$; $2,\tfrac18,-8,-1$; and so on.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Condition 4.1 and Equations (5)–(8), with supplement Equation (3): corrected well-definedness and first-moment unbiasedness under a targeted first-moment condition
canonical_claim.location: p. 6 (PDF p. 6) and p. 7 (PDF p. 7); Supplementary Appendix p. 2 (publisher-supplement.pdf p. 2); the general claims qualified are on p. 2 (PDF p. 2) and p. 14 (PDF p. 14)
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: Setting: (S1)–(S4). $\pi_i(d)$, Condition 4.1, Equation (5): p. 6 (S5). Equations (6)–(8): p. 7 (S6). Condition 5.1: p. 8 (S7). $\hat{\overline y}(d)$: supplement Equation (1), p. 1 (S8). $Y_i=y_i(\mathbf Z)$ (S3). $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)$ as in (S10)(a); it is countable by (S1). Expectations are sums over $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)$ weighted by $\Pr[\mathbf Z=\mathbf z]$, and conditional expectations given $D_i=d$ use the weights $\Pr[\mathbf Z=\mathbf z]/\pi_i(d)$ on $\{\mathbf z:g_i(\mathbf z)=d\}$. The claims qualified, as printed: p. 2 “these targets remain well-defined as combinations of potential outcomes, even under interference or misspecification of exposures—as long as the design is known”; p. 14 “These quantities remain well-defined under arbitrary interference or exposure misspecification”; supplement p. 2 “it is finite-N unbiased for the AEPO” (P061-T11, P061-T16).
canonical_claim.note: Steps 11–17 of the validator's derivation; the prior correction's text was judged correct. The repair is a minor regularity condition that changes no estimand and no number in the paper: it holds in every finite-support example (the rebel-group survey, the school experiment, Tables 1–5, the sampling–treatment designs) and under NURVA at the targeted exposures. The condition is targeted: it is required only at the exposures used in a target, and it is weaker than integrability of $Y_i$. The validator also shows that it is necessary for $\overline y_i(d)$ to be a finite ordinary (signed) mean, and that restricting to finite support would be a sufficient but narrower repair; neither is part of this target. The same missing condition affects the AEPO term in supplement Equation (10) (P061-T20), whose proof needs in addition finite expectations of the predictions. The counterexample to the uncorrected claim is P061-T7; the validator's bounded comparison on the same design ($y_1(k)=(-1)^{k+1}$) has $M_{1,1}=\tfrac12$ and $\overline y_1(1)=\mathrm E[\hat{\overline y}(1)]=\tfrac13$. This finding also affects headline claim P061-H5.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Section 6.3 (Generalizing across sampling–treatment designs): the passage with its notation corrected
canonical_claim.statement:
Section 6.3 with the notation repaired (Sol's smallest repair: both occurrences of $y_i(d)$ replaced by $\overline y_i(d)$, $g_i(z)$ by $g_i(\mathbf z)$, and the first $\tau_{Z'}(2,1)$ by $\tau_{\mathbf Z'}(2,1)$): ‘Within a finite population of size $N$, consider a design $\mathbf Z$ that first draws a simple random sample of size $n$ without replacement and then, among sampled units, assigns $k$ to treatment and $n-k$ to control by complete randomization. Define an exposure mapping where $z_i=2$ indicates that unit $i$ is sampled and treated, $z_i=1$ that it is sampled and untreated and $z_i=0$ that it is not sampled. We can define the AEED, $\tau_{\mathbf Z}(2,1)$ which, under NURVA, admits a causal interpretation as the effect, under this joint sampling-assignment design, of exposing a unit to being “sampled and treated” rather than “sampled and untreated.” Now consider a different design $\mathbf Z'$ on the same population, with sample size $n'$ and number treated $k'$. Using the same exposure mapping, define the corresponding AEED $\tau_{\mathbf Z'}(2,1)$. We define the exposure mapping as $$g_i(\mathbf z)=\begin{cases}2&:z_i=2\\1&:z_i=1\\0&:z_i=0\end{cases},\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,N\},\mathbf z\in\mathcal Z.$$ Even if NURVA holds for both $\mathbf Z$ and $\mathbf Z'$, there is no guarantee that $\tau_{\mathbf Z}(2,1)$ will equal $\tau_{\mathbf Z'}(2,1)$: changing either $n$ to $n'$ or $k$ to $k'$ changes the distribution of other units’ sampling or treatment statuses conditional on $D_i=d$, and hence may change the EPOs $\overline y_i(d)$ that enter the AEPOs. Learning what would happen under alternative values of $(n,k)$ or in alternative target populations requires additional stability assumptions on how $\overline y_i(d)$ varies with the sampling and treatment scheme’. Footnote 10: ‘Support under the two designs: $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)=\mathrm{Sym}((\underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{k},\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{n-k},\underbrace{0,\ldots,0}_{N-n}))$, $\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z')=\mathrm{Sym}((\underbrace{2,\ldots,2}_{k'},\underbrace{1,\ldots,1}_{n'-k'},\underbrace{0,\ldots,0}_{N-n'}))$.’
Formal content of the corrected claim. Let $\mathbf Z$ be uniform on $\mathrm{Sym}((2^{k},1^{n-k},0^{N-n}))$ and $\mathbf Z'$ uniform on $\mathrm{Sym}((2^{k'},1^{n'-k'},0^{N-n'}))$, with $g_i(\mathbf z)=z_i$ on $\mathcal Z\supseteq\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z)\cup\mathrm{Supp}(\mathbf Z')$. There exist $N$, raw potential outcomes on $\mathcal Z$ and $(n,k)\ne(n',k')$ such that Condition 4.1 holds for the exposures 2 and 1 under both designs, Condition 5.1 (NURVA) holds under $\mathbf Z$ and under $\mathbf Z'$, and $\tau_{\mathbf Z}(2,1)\ne\tau_{\mathbf Z'}(2,1)$. Witness: $N=4$, $\mathcal Z=\{0,1,2\}^4$, $y_i(\mathbf z)=\#\{j:z_j>0\}\cdot\mathbb 1\{z_i=2\}$, $(n,k)=(2,1)$ and $(n',k')=(3,1)$. Under the design with sample size $n$, $y_i(\mathbf z)=n\,\mathbb 1\{z_i=2\}$ on the support, so $\overline y_i(2)=n$ and $\overline y_i(1)=0$ for every $i$; hence $\tau_{\mathbf Z}(2,1)=2$ and $\tau_{\mathbf Z'}(2,1)=3$, NURVA holds under each design, and SUTVA (Condition 5.2) fails on $\mathcal Z$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: $\mathrm{Sym}(\cdot)$: p. 3, “where $\mathrm{Sym}(\cdot)$ represents the set/orbit of distinct permutations of a vector”. The joint sampling–treatment design: a simple random sample of size $n$ without replacement followed by complete randomization of $k$ of the sampled units to treatment, which is the uniform distribution on $\mathrm{Sym}((2^k,1^{n-k},0^{N-n}))$, a set of $N!/(k!\,(n-k)!\,(N-n)!)$ assignments; $2^k$ abbreviates $k$ coordinates equal to 2 (not the paper's notation). $\overline y_i(d)$: Equation (5), p. 6 (S5); AEPO and AEED: Equations (6) and (8), p. 7 (S6); the subscripts in $\tau_{\mathbf Z}$, $\tau_{\mathbf Z'}$ name the design under which the AEED is computed (p. 6: the definitions “could be augmented (e.g., $\overline y_i(d;(g,\mathbf Z))$) to facilitate comparisons across different designs and exposure mappings”). Conditions 5.1, 5.2: p. 8 (S7), read as in (S10)(d). As printed (p. 13): ‘define the corresponding AEED $\tau_{Z'}(2,1)$’ with an italic $Z'$; ‘$g_i(z)=\ldots$’ with an italic argument $z$ beside the bold $\mathbf z\in\mathcal Z$; and ‘the EPOs $y_i(d)$ that enter the AEPOs’ and ‘how $y_i(d)$ varies’ without the overbar.
canonical_claim.note: P061-N008 is rated an error, Minor (ratings.json): misprinted symbols in a formula and in two references to the EPO; Sol's verdict is confirmed by a page check (font records in _batch/P061-B02/work/page13_fonts.json), and the design-dependence argument is unaffected. The corrected passage is prose around one display, so its formal content is fixed here as an existence statement, which is what ‘there is no guarantee that … will equal …’ asserts. The witness is not in the paper, which gives no table for Section 6.3: it is the example constructed by the Opus reader when checking headline claim P061-H4 (recorded in merge/candidates.json: $N=4$, treated outcome equal to the number sampled, $\tau(2,1)=2$ against 3), recomputed in exact arithmetic when this list was fixed (both supports have 12 assignments; NURVA holds under each design; SUTVA fails on $\{0,1,2\}^4$). A Lean statement can certify the witness and, if wanted, the mechanism named in the passage: conditional on $Z_i=2$ the other $N-1$ coordinates are uniform over the arrangements of $k-1$ twos, $n-k$ ones and $N-n$ zeros, a law that depends on $(n,k)$. It cannot certify the last quoted sentence (‘requires additional stability assumptions’), which is interpretive.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Supplementary Appendix, ‘Central limit theorems’ paragraph and the paragraph on limitations: the two degree rates with the population index corrected
canonical_claim.statement:
The two sentences with the index repaired (Sol's smallest repair: $o(N^{1/4})$ and $O(N^{1/2})$ in place of $o(n^{1/4})$ and $O(n^{1/2})$): ‘Recent advancements in this area have been made under weakened assumptions about the growth of the maximum degree in the dependency graph, specifically that the maximum degree $d_{\max}$ grows at a rate of $o(N^{1/4})$ (Ogburn et al. 2024; Han, Basse, and Bojinov 2024).’ and ‘Sävje, Aronow, and Hudgens (2021) prove that Chebyshev’s inequality remains asymptotically sharp under strong restrictions on the growth of the degree sequence, even when the average degree $d_{\mathrm{avg}}$ is $O(1)$ and the maximum degree $d_{\max}$ is $O(N^{1/2})$.’
Formal content. Along the supplement's sequence of finite populations $U_{(N)}$ indexed by the population size $N$ (p. 5), with $d_{\max,(N)}$ and $d_{\mathrm{avg},(N)}$ the maximum and the average degree of the dependency graph on the $N$ units of $U_{(N)}$, the three rate conditions are, as $N\to\infty$: $d_{\max,(N)}/N^{1/4}\to0$; $\sup_Nd_{\mathrm{avg},(N)}<\infty$; and $\sup_Nd_{\max,(N)}/N^{1/2}<\infty$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The asymptotic sequence indexed by $N$: supplement p. 5 (S9). As printed (supplement p. 6): ‘grows at a rate of $o(n^{1/4})$’ and ‘the maximum degree $d_{\max}$ is $O(n^{1/2})$’, with a lower-case $n$ that the supplement uses elsewhere for the number of units sampled into exposure $d$ (p. 1: “a simple random sampling strategy of $n$ of $N$ units into exposure $d$”). The dependency graph, $d_{\max}$ and $d_{\mathrm{avg}}$ are not defined in the supplement beyond the words quoted (“the maximum degree in the dependency graph”, “the average degree $d_{\mathrm{avg}}$”); in the cited literature the dependency graph joins units whose exposure and outcome variables are dependent. $o(\cdot)$ and $O(\cdot)$ are the usual order symbols for sequences indexed by $N$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: None: the corrected sentences state rate conditions and attribute results to other works; no proof in the paper rests on them.
canonical_claim.note: P061-N011 is rated an error, Minor (ratings.json): a symbol slip in two rate expressions, confirmed by a page check; nothing depends on it. It is on the list because the author's instruction covers every confirmed error in a formula, including a misprinted symbol. The corrected sentences contain no proposition of the paper's own: they describe hypotheses and results of cited works. A Lean formalization can therefore only state the three rate conditions as predicates on sequences indexed by the population size, and the point of fidelity is that index ($N$, not the supplement's $n$). The only mathematical relation between the corrected displays is that the first rate implies the third ($d_{\max,(N)}=o(N^{1/4})$ implies $d_{\max,(N)}=O(N^{1/2})$); the paper does not assert it, and it is mentioned only as a possible sanity lemma. Whether the cited works state these rates and results is finding P061-N012 (undetermined as to the Bickel–Freedman reference; the degree-rate and sharpness allegations not confirmed) and is outside this target; the cited works are not staged. The paragraph is listed among the related candidates of headline claim P061-H6, but the rating records no headline claim as affected.
